correctness.rationale: Every powered-distance eigenvalue is obtained explicitly from Fourier character sums of the three distance shells. The only potentially nonnegative nonconstant blocks are the parity character F_{q,d} and the first-order Fourier shell -2^p+M(3^p-1). The derivative of F has at most one maximum, and the first root criterion gives the exact exponent and kernel multiplicities. For q/d tending to alpha, expansion on p<=b_1 uses N b_1^2->0, proving the two asymptotic regimes and constant alpha_c. A standalone checker constructs actual graph shortest paths independently and verifies 28 full character spectra and five critical nullities; finite checks are not treated as proof.

evidence: The categorical product is the bipartite double cover of the direct graph product of d complete q-vertex graphs. Its metric is an abelian Cayley metric on a group of order 2q^d.
Murugan 2011 Theorem 3.1 converts the supremal exponent to the first zero of a vertex-transitive distance determinant; no product-specific roots are stated.

value.rationale: The object is a natural vertex-transitive graph metric on categorical powers, whose Hilbert snowflake exponent is a meaningful geometric embedding invariant. The classification identifies exactly two otherwise competing obstructions, their full Fourier multiplicities and endpoint embedding dimensions; the asymptotic switch at alpha_c approximately 1.003242 and the additional factor of q in the exponent on one side are neither a parameter-renaming exercise nor inferred from finite examples.
